issues.description: Field: SealSaloon.stock — The problem statement (lines 70-71) instructs students to add a final Stock stock that is initialized in the SealSaloon constructor (implying an instance field initialized at construction). Elsewhere in the same problem statement (lines 77-81) it explicitly requires that the stock attribute must be static and shared across all SealSaloon instances. The solution implements this field as a static declaration (private static final Stock stock = new Stock()). These conflicting requirements (instance-final initialized in constructor vs. static-final initialized at declaration) leave students unsure which design to implement and whether to initialize the field in the constructor or at declaration.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the contradiction by choosing one design and updating all artifacts. Recommended resolution: make stock a shared resource and state in the problem statement and UML that stock is static (e.g., "private static final Stock stock"). Instruct students to initialize it at declaration or in a static initializer (not in the constructor). Update the UML and prose to remove the instruction to initialize stock in the constructor. Alternatively, if an instance-scoped stock was intended, remove the 'must be static' notes and keep the constructor initialization guidance. Ensure the solution, template, and problem text match the chosen design.

issues.description: Method: SealSaloon.checkOrderReady — The UML and prose in the problem statement (UML line shows +checkOrderReady(): void and the ordering text describes calling checkOrderReady() with no arguments) declare a no-argument method checkOrderReady(). The solution, however, implements public void checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging). This parameter mismatch between the specified no-arg signature and the solution's boolean-parameter signature confuses students about which method signature to implement and how orderMeal should invoke it.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: keep the no-argument signature in the specification and update the solution to implement public void checkOrderReady() (remove the enableLogging parameter) and adjust any internal logging to use a private helper if needed (e.g., private void checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) called by the public no-arg method). Alternatively, if the boolean flag is intended for debugging, document it in the problem statement and UML and provide an overload or default behavior in the spec.
